verses.english: One in whom no sensualities dwell; in whom no craving is found; who has crossed over perplexity— his emancipation: What is it like? The Buddha: One in whom no sensualities dwell; in whom no craving is found; who has crossed over perplexity— his emancipation is not other than that. Todeyya: Is he without desire, or desiring? Discerning or still acquiring discernment? Describe the sage to me, Sakyan, All-around Eye, so that I may recognize what he is like. The Buddha: He’s without desire, not desiring; discerning, not still acquiring discernment. Recognize the sage, Todeyya, as having nothing, unentangled in sensuality & becoming.
